{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZd6UJA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDFGkU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 47, "title": "Correct WD2793 Type-I per-step movement, timing and interruption", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `843a0861af7818e4a28405f039a81f984576a58d`, `crates/msx-core/src/disk.rs:338` assigns every seek one distance-independent delay using approximately 6/12/18/30 ms. At completion, `tick()` applies the entire head/register change atomically. Consequently, a 79-track seek completes like a one-track seek, intermediate movement is invisible, and FORCE INTERRUPT loses movement that should already have occurred.

`crates/msx-core/tests/disk.rs` currently accepts that 79-track seek after only 228,000 CPU cycles, approximately 64 ms. This is incorrect shared controller behavior affecting firmware polling, cancellation and subsequent sector addressing. No particular commercial-title failure is established.

## Expected outcome

Execute RESTORE, SEEK and STEP-family movement incrementally at the selected rate, preserving completed movement when interrupted. Both existing disk interfaces must observe the same corrected controller through their existing wiring.

## Context

The checkout is clean and matches inspected GitHub main. Open Issues/PRs are empty. [Issue #41](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/issues/41) and [PR #42](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/pull/42) added Philips interface coexistence; this task corrects the shared movement engine.

Inspected references:

- [TI second-source TMS279X/WD279X manual](https://deramp.com/swtpc.com/DC_5/TMS279X_DataSheet.pdf), printed pages 12–13 and 17: rate table, movement, track updates and track-zero behavior. This is an edited transcription of second-source manufacturer documentation, without physical-device confirmation.
- [Pinned openMSX WD2793 implementation](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/fdc/WD2793.cc), `startType1Cmd`, `seek`, `step` and `seekNext`: corroborates incremental execution and supplies an explicit scheduling reference. Its verification sequence contains a TODO.

The original WD scan remained technically unreadable through available extraction/screenshots; another handbook exceeded the fetch size limit. Those references establish no additional facts.

Scope is movement and its observable timing within the current instruction-boundary scheduler. Retain the existing verification-result predicate after movement, documenting that verification settling/rotational search, READY-independent Type-I execution, head-load fidelity and exact internal command latency remain separate gaps. Sector-transfer timing and unsupported commands remain outside this change.

Existing native disk/Philips tests provide coverage. [PR #46](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/pull/46) reports 176 Rust and 98 browser passes; its [CI job](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/actions/runs/40007010240/job/120597372888) records successful suite steps. These results do not validate the proposed movement traces. No application checks were rerun during planning.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Replace atomic target assignment with incremental RESTORE/SEEK/STEP execution. Use 6/12/20/30 ms intervals for the selected 1 MHz controller profile. Document conversion to the 3,579,545 Hz CPU clock and rounding; prevent accumulated timing drift and consume all elapsed movement events independently of `tick()` chunk size.
- [ ] Adopt the pinned upstream scheduling convention within the current timing model: issue the first eligible step at command start, subsequent steps at rate intervals, and finish after the final interval. With V=0, equal Track/Data emits no steps and needs no artificial step delay. A synchronized 0→79 seek at rate 00 therefore lasts approximately 474 ms, rather than 6 ms. Label omitted internal startup latency explicitly.
- [ ] Preserve head/register separation, remembered STEP direction and T-controlled updates. SEEK follows the register delta without silently repairing a head offset. RESTORE follows the track-zero sensor and repairs the register; outward movement at zero must not wrap. Document and test the bounded drive's upper-limit/error policy without discarding completed movement or aliasing invalid tracks into valid sectors.
- [ ] Keep BUSY asserted throughout scheduled movement, DRQ clear and completion IRQ correctly timed. FORCE INTERRUPT cancels future steps while retaining already issued movement/register changes; subsequent ticks must not resurrect the command. Preserve existing signal acknowledgement/polarity and disconnected CPU IRQ. Existing abort/reset/media/profile-removal paths must cancel pending movement and retain their documented lifecycle behavior.
- [ ] Add independently calculated traces for all rates, distances 0/1/5/79, both directions, RESTORE, STEP/T variants, mismatched head/register positions and drive boundaries. Check immediately before/at/after events, interruption between steps, and equivalent large/irregular/single-cycle tick partitions. Infer physical position through track-zero status and subsequent sector access where practical. Correct obsolete fixed-wait expectations; retain verification-result and partial-write regressions. Record meaningful baseline failures and corrected results.
- [ ] Add an original CPU-executed Philips-register probe on both models that observes intermediate progress, interrupts a multi-step seek and successfully addresses the resulting position. Exercise compiled Wasm through existing browser tooling at both hosting roots. Preserve Weave disk boot, firmware/sub-ROM/mapper coexistence, private disk ownership/export, dirty-media protection, SRAM persistence and existing video/audio/input behavior. Maintain provenance for any changed generated fixtures.
- [ ] Update `docs/disks.md` and affected timing documentation. The Coordinator runs and reports `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, `npm test` and `git diff --check`, using README dependency setup as needed. Complete source-Issue/full-diff review and resolve blocking findings before merge. Distinguish passing, failing, skipped and unperformed checks.

## Optional validation

Compare original timestamped traces with the pinned upstream implementation. Record additional software checks using already lawfully available inputs separately. Proprietary acquisition, physical hardware and human gameplay are unnecessary; authored diagnostics do not establish commercial compatibility.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
